data.title: Suspicious "final warning before seizure" for broadcasting fees (€254.35)
data.summary: A letter dated 26 September 2026 from a "Rundfunk Zahlungszentrale" demands €254.35 in broadcasting fees within 48 hours of receipt. It threatens account and wage seizure and asks for payment to a Lithuanian IBAN. It has several signs of a scam.
data.explanation: This letter looks like a scam, or at least needs checking before you pay anything. The real fee service (Beitragsservice) does not normally demand payment within 48 hours. It does not normally use foreign accounts or tell you not to contact its usual address. The IBAN is Lithuanian (LT) and the payee is a "UAB", which is a Lithuanian company form. Don't pay and don't reply by the e-mail given. Instead, check your fee account through the official Beitragsservice website or the contact details from your earlier letters. If it is fake, you can report it to the police or a consumer advice centre.

items.title: Verify the demand before paying
items.action: Check with the official Beitragsservice (using contact details from earlier genuine letters, not this one) whether you owe any arrears. Do not pay to the IBAN in this letter until confirmed.
items.consequence: The letter threatens seizure of account and wages, but this is unverified and may be a scam.

warnings: The payment account is a Lithuanian IBAN (LT) and the payee is a 'UAB', which does not fit a German broadcasting fee service.
A 48-hour deadline with threats of seizure and no further notice is a typical pressure tactic.
The letter tells you not to write to the known Beitragsservice address and to use only an unfamiliar e-mail address.
The sender name differs from your known Beitragsservice Musterstadt, and the greeting 'Sehr geehrte Herr Rivera' and the spaced-out signature look unprofessional.
A genuine enforcement process would normally come from the fee service with an official notice, not a 'last warning' with a foreign bank account.
